title: The canonical Cech augmentation of a size-aligned injective sheaf is a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let C have v-small Hom sets and finite wide pullbacks, and let J admit sheafification for v-small abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let I be an injective abelian sheaf [def-sp-injective-resolutions], X an object, and pi_i:U_i -> X a v-small family generating a covering sieve. Let L be its Mathlib alternating Cech complex, using categorical products in Over X [def-sc-cech-resolution-double-complex]. For any chain map e from I(X) concentrated in degree zero to L, assume that for every tuple t:Fin 1 -> iota, projection of e.f 0 to the t-factor is restriction along the structural arrow from the corresponding product to X. Then e is a quasi-isomorphism. This assertion involves one sheaf and no double complex or totalization.

source.place: Lemma 21.10.2, together with Lemma 21.10.1 (03F6) and the canonical degree-zero identification (03AN); blueprint sk-thm-picard-cech Step 3.

proof.text: Construct the augmented free abelian presheaf complex of the covering, using the same categorical fibre products as Mathlib. The representable basis sets are v-small because Hom sets are v-small; their coproducts are v-small because the tuple-index type is v-small. Its augmentation targets the free abelian representable of X. On a localization where an arrow into X lifts to a covering member, insertion of that lift at the beginning of tuples contracts the augmented complex. The covering sieve ensures these localizations cover, hence the sheafified augmented complex is exact. Sheafification is exact and the augmentation becomes an epimorphism.

Apply Hom into I to this exact complex of abelian sheaves. At any cocycle degree, the map out of the free term factors through the image of its boundary; injectivity extends that factor to the preceding term, yielding a coboundary. The free abelian representable adjunction identifies these Hom groups with I evaluated on each fibre product, and Hom out of coproducts with products. Precomposing the alternating face maps gives precisely the alternating coface differential in Mathlib. Thus positive Cech cohomology is zero and the augmented degree-zero kernel is the image of I(X).

The sheaf condition says that compatible sections on the covering uniquely descend to X. Through the single-factor product isomorphisms, the canonical restriction map identifies I(X) with the degree-zero kernel. Projection uniqueness and he identify e.f 0 with that restriction map. Since the source complex is concentrated in degree zero, this gives an isomorphism on degree-zero homology and the zero-object isomorphisms in all positive degrees. If the cover is empty, the sheaf condition gives I(X)=0 and all Cech terms are zero.
